questions.title: Headcount
questions.story_md:
How many people could get in your way, and what do they cost?

For the **{dept}** department return two columns: the **number of employees** and their **total salary**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(salary) FROM employees WHERE dept = {dept|sql};

questions.title: Total Haul
questions.story_md:
What is zone **{zone}** worth?

Return the **total value** of all items stored there.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(value) FROM vault_items WHERE zone = {zone|sql};

questions.title: Average Paycheck
questions.story_md:
Know what a bribe needs to beat.

Return the **average salary** of **{dept}** employees, **rounded to 2 decimals**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) FROM employees WHERE dept = {dept|sql};

questions.title: Richest and Poorest
questions.story_md:
Scope the range of targets.

Return two columns: the **highest** and the **lowest** balance among **{type}** accounts.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT MAX(balance), MIN(balance) FROM accounts WHERE type = {type|sql};

hints.text: MAX() and MIN() can be in one SELECT.

questions.title: Shop Count
questions.story_md:
How active is account **{account}**?

Return two columns: its **number of transactions** and the **number of distinct merchants** it paid (`COUNT(DISTINCT …)` ignores missing merchants).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT merchant) FROM transactions WHERE account_id = {account};

hints.text: COUNT(DISTINCT col) skips duplicates and NULLs.

questions.title: Last Alarm
questions.story_md:
When did zone **{zone}** last go off?

Return the **latest triggered date** for alarms in that zone.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT MAX(triggered) FROM alarms WHERE zone = {zone|sql};

hints.text: MAX works on YYYY-MM-DD text too.

questions.title: Van Capacity
questions.story_md:
Can the van carry all the **{item}** items?

Return their **total weight in kg, rounded to 1 decimal**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(weight_kg), 1) FROM vault_items WHERE item = {item|sql};

questions.title: Withdrawal Pattern
questions.story_md:
Profile the withdrawals.

Return three columns for transactions of kind **withdrawal**: the **count**, the **total amount**, and the **average amount rounded to 2 decimals**.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount), ROUND(AVG(amount), 2) FROM transactions WHERE kind = 'withdrawal';

questions.title: Team Sizes
questions.story_md:
Who has the most people?

Return **dept** and the **number of employees** in each department.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT dept, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY dept;

questions.title: Zone Values
questions.story_md:
Rank the zones by loot.

Return **zone** and the **total item value** for each zone.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT zone, SUM(value) FROM vault_items GROUP BY zone;

questions.title: Account Types
questions.story_md:
Which account type holds the most per account?

Return **type** and the **average balance rounded to 2 decimals** for each account type.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT type, ROUND(AVG(balance), 2) FROM accounts GROUP BY type;

questions.title: Alarm Levels
questions.story_md:
Measure how jumpy the system is.

Return **level** and the **number of alarms** at that level in zone **{zone}**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT level, COUNT(*) FROM alarms WHERE zone = {zone|sql} GROUP BY level;

questions.title: Spending Map
questions.story_md:
Follow the money of account **{account}**.

Return **merchant** and **total amount** spent there (skip rows with no merchant).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT merchant, SUM(amount) FROM transactions WHERE account_id = {account} AND merchant IS NOT NULL GROUP BY merchant;

questions.title: Hiring Waves
questions.story_md:
When did the bank hire most?

Return the **year** (as text, e.g. `2019`) and the **number of employees hired** that year.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', hired), COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY strftime('%Y', hired);

questions.title: Loan Book
questions.story_md:
Who owes the bank money?

Return **status**, the **number of loans** and their **total amount** for each loan status.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE loans (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, rate REAL, status TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM loans GROUP BY status;

questions.title: Branch Staffing
questions.story_md:
Plan who is in which building.

Return **branch_id**, **dept** and the **number of employees** for every branch/department combination.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT branch_id, dept, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY branch_id, dept;

hints.text: GROUP BY can take several columns.

questions.title: Busy Zones
questions.story_md:
Avoid zones with lots of alarms.

Return **zone** and **alarm count** for zones with **more than {n}** alarms.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT zone, COUNT(*) FROM alarms GROUP BY zone HAVING COUNT(*) > {n};

hints.text: HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY.

questions.title: Rich Departments
questions.story_md:
Where is the payroll concentrated?

Return **dept** and **average salary (rounded to 2 decimals)** for departments whose average salary is **above {avg}**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT dept, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) FROM employees GROUP BY dept HAVING AVG(salary) > {avg};

questions.title: Regulars
questions.story_md:
Find accounts that move money a lot.

Return **account_id** and **number of transactions** for accounts with **at least {n}** transactions.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) FROM transactions GROUP BY account_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= {n};

questions.title: Worth the Trip
questions.story_md:
Only item types worth a lot in total are worth carrying.

Return **item** and **total value** for item types whose total value exceeds **{total}**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT item, SUM(value) FROM vault_items GROUP BY item HAVING SUM(value) > {total};

questions.title: Open Alarms by Zone
questions.story_md:
Count only the alarms nobody has dealt with.

Return **zone** and the **number of unresolved alarms** (`resolved = 0`) for zones with **at least {n}** of them.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT zone, COUNT(*) FROM alarms WHERE resolved = 0 GROUP BY zone HAVING COUNT(*) >= {n};

questions.title: Target Tiers
questions.story_md:
Label every account.

Return **id** and a **band**: `high` if balance ≥ **{high}**, `mid` if balance ≥ **{mid}**, otherwise `low`.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, CASE WHEN balance >= {high} THEN 'high' WHEN balance >= {mid} THEN 'mid' ELSE 'low' END FROM accounts;

questions.title: Band Sizes
questions.story_md:
How many targets are in each band?

Using the bands `heavy` (weight_kg ≥ **{heavy}**) and `light` (everything else), return **band** and **number of items** in each band.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN weight_kg >= {heavy} THEN 'heavy' ELSE 'light' END, COUNT(*) FROM vault_items GROUP BY CASE WHEN weight_kg >= {heavy} THEN 'heavy' ELSE 'light' END;

hints.text: You can GROUP BY a CASE expression (or its alias).

questions.title: In and Out
questions.story_md:
Net flow for account **{account}**.

Return two columns: the **total of deposits** and the **total of withdrawals** for that account (0 if none).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'deposit' THEN amount ELSE 0 END), SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'withdrawal' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) FROM transactions WHERE account_id = {account};

hints.text: SUM(CASE WHEN kind = … THEN amount ELSE 0 END)

questions.title: Name Badges
questions.story_md:
Print fake badges.

Return **id** and the **full name** as `first_name last_name` (one space between) for **{dept}** employees.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, first_name || ' ' || last_name FROM employees WHERE dept = {dept|sql};

questions.title: Long Names
questions.story_md:
Long last names are easy to spot on a list.

Return **last_name** and its **length** for employees whose last name is **longer than {n}** characters.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT last_name, LENGTH(last_name) FROM employees WHERE LENGTH(last_name) > {n};

hints.text: LENGTH(text) returns the number of characters.

questions.title: Initials
questions.story_md:
Codenames are initials.

Return **id** and **initials** — first letter of first_name followed by first letter of last_name, in UPPER case (e.g. `AB`) — for employees on branch **{branch}**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, UPPER(SUBSTR(first_name, 1, 1) || SUBSTR(last_name, 1, 1)) FROM employees WHERE branch_id = {branch};

questions.title: Monthly Volume
questions.story_md:
Spot the busiest month.

Return the **month** as `YYYY-MM` and the **total amount** of **{kind}** transactions in that month.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', at), SUM(amount) FROM transactions WHERE kind = {kind|sql} GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', at);

questions.title: Old Timers
questions.story_md:
Veterans know the vault codes.

Return **id** and **days employed** as of **2026-01-01** (whole days, e.g. via `julianday`) for employees hired before **{before}**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, CAST(julianday('2026-01-01') - julianday(hired) AS INTEGER) FROM employees WHERE hired < {before|sql};

hints.text: julianday(a) - julianday(b) gives days between dates.
CAST(… AS INTEGER) drops the fraction.

questions.title: Weekend Shift
questions.story_md:
Fewer guards on weekends.

Return **id** and **triggered** of alarms raised on a **Saturday or Sunday**. (In SQLite, `strftime('%w', d)` is `0` for Sunday and `6` for Saturday.)
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, triggered FROM alarms WHERE strftime('%w', triggered) IN ('0', '6');
